title: Phage DNA Extraction with Phenol-Chloroform and Digestion to Single Nucleosides
author: Adair Borges
materials: To degrade any non-encapsulated nucleic acids, treat the concentrated phage lysate with 10 µg/mL RNase A (NEB T3018) and 10 µg/mL DNase I (NEB M0303). Digest for 1 h at room temperature or 4 °C overnight. Store phage at 4 °C.
Strip away phage capsids with 1 µl of Proteinase K (NEB P8107S) + 0.05% SDS. Incubate at 55 °C for 60 minutes on a Thermomixer at 250 rpm. If you only have a static heat block, vortex every 10 min.

In fume hood, add an equal volume of phenol – chloroform – isoamyl alcohol mixture, pH 8 (Sigma Aldrich 77618) to the digested phage. If the volume of phage is low, consider bringing up the volume to 500 µl with 1x TE buffer. Incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes, vortexing regularly to keep phenol mixed in.
Use a Nucleoside Digestion Mix (NEB - M0649S) to digest 1 µg of DNA. Each reaction should contain 1 µL of Nucleoside Digestion Mix and 2 µL of 10× Nucleoside Digestion Mix buffer.

steps.title: Initial Sample Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Spin the sample at maximum speed at 4 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Chloroform Extraction
steps.instruction: Perform aqueous layer extraction using chloroform in a fume hood.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the aqueous layer (top layer) to a new tube, avoiding the interface and any debris or organics.
Add an equal volume of chloroform to the sample and invert to mix.
Spin the sample at maximum speed at 4 °C for 5 minutes.
Repeat the extraction process by transferring the aqueous layer and repeating the chloroform wash.

steps.title: DNA Precipitation
steps.instruction: Precipitate the DNA using sodium acetate and isopropanol.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the aqueous layer to a new tube.
Add a 10% volume of 3 M sodium acetate and an equal volume of isopropanol to the sample.
Invert to mix and incubate at 4 °C for 2 hours (or overnight).
Spin the sample at maximum speed at 4 °C for 30 minutes.

steps.title: DNA Pellet Washing
steps.instruction: Wash the DNA pellet to remove residual salts and solvents.

substeps.instruction: Carefully pipette off the liquid, leaving the glassy smear or pellet.
Wash the pellet with 1 mL freshly-made 70% ethanol (room temperature); ensure any DNA stuck to the tube sides is washed down.
Spin the sample at maximum speed at 4 °C for 5 minutes.
Carefully pipette off the liquid and wash with 500 µl of 70% ethanol.
Spin the sample at maximum speed at 4 °C for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Ethanol Removal and Drying
steps.instruction: Completely remove ethanol and dry the pellet.

substeps.instruction: Carefully pipette off the liquid.
Perform short spins and pipette with progressively smaller volumes until all ethanol is removed.
Let the pellet dry for 5 minutes or less.

steps.title: DNA Resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the DNA pellet in nuclease-free water.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 30 µl of nuclease-free water (adjust volume if a large DNA yield is anticipated).
Optionally warm the sample to 50 °C to aid resuspension.

steps.title: Digestion to Single Nucleosides
steps.instruction: Digest the DNA and inactivate the enzyme.

substeps.instruction: Perform reactions in a 20 µL total volume.
Incubate at 37 °C for 1 hour.
Inactivate the enzyme by heating at 80 °C for 15 minutes.
Store digested samples at 4 °C until downstream use or analysis.
